A schemaVersion respelled as true or "1" therefore does not fail -- it mints a DIFFERENT, complete, correctly framed capability manifest id over the wrong manifest. This is IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 6 law 18's exact defect class reachable inside this recipe, and it is why ADM-TYPE is a gate BEFORE encoding rather than a property of the encoder.

admission.rule: FOUR GATES, ALL BEFORE ENCODING. A value that fails any gate is not a CapabilityManifestV1, is not committed, and has no capabilityManifestId. Nothing is normalised at a consumer, ever.

Every vector in this document publishes its COMPLETE violation list in this order, so nothing depends on which violation is first.

ADM-TYPE.statement: Every scalar is admitted by EXACT JSON TYPE before its content is compared. schemaVersion is a JSON integer -- a boolean is not an integer, a float is not an integer, a numeric string is not a number -- and every other declared scalar is a JSON string. The type assertion is the gate; content comparison happens only after it passes.
ADM-TYPE.source: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 6 law 18. Not a restatement for decoration: NEG-TYPE-1 and NEG-TYPE-2 show this recipe is REACHABLE by the class, because CVE1 is total on booleans and on strings and mints a wrong id rather than failing.
ADM-TYPE.andITISENFORCEDBYARETAINEDCHECKER: check-delivery-v4.py implements the gate with `type(x) is int`, never isinstance, and its --selftest mutates that single expression to `isinstance(x, int)` and REQUIRES the run to fail. Law 18 defeated C-2 at v3, v5, v6, v7 and v8 successively, each time inside the repair's own self-certification, and a sibling reintroduced it through the generator written to fix a blocker. A gate that cannot be shown to fail is not a gate.
ADM-TYPE.whatITCANNOTDO: a digest cannot police its own input's type. An implementation that coerces 1.0 to 1 before calling the encoder produces the CORRECT id and has still violated law 18.

ADM-CLOSED.statement: EVERY REACHABLE RECORD IS CLOSED, AND A MAP IS NOT A RECORD. Every JSON object reachable from a committed CapabilityManifestV1 -- the record itself, every element of every declared collection, every value of every declared map, and every object a later successor adds at any depth -- is either a RECORD or a MAP, and the schema says which by what it declares for it. A RECORD declares a KEY SET: it carries EXACTLY that key set, each key exactly once, with no undeclared member. A MAP declares a KEY DOMAIN: it carries no key set, closure does not apply to it, its keys are admitted by DL-DOM-1 against that domain, and its VALUES are governed by this property recursively -- so a map of records is closed at its records and A MAP WHOSE VALUES ARE SCALARS CLOSES NOTHING. A reachable object type that declares NEITHER a key set NOR a key domain is a schema defect and is inadmissible until it declares one; permissiveness is never the default.
ADM-CLOSED.whyITMATTERSUNDERCVE1: an undeclared key is not silently dropped by CVE1 -- it changes the id. So an open reading is still injective, and the defect is different and worse than loss: a mistyped key ships a manifest that a human reads as unchanged under an id that has moved. Closing the record turns that into a refusal.
ADM-CLOSED.changeFromThePredecessor: delivery.v2 declares `closed: true` on CapabilityManifestV1 only. This narrows the two nested records to match. It is a narrowing: every manifest admissible after this change was admissible before.
ADM-CLOSED.changeFromTheREJECTEDCANDIDATE: delivery.v3's statement of this gate is the subject of blocker IR-V3-B1. Its enumeration reaches a declared map's VALUES and its catch-all reaches the MAP, and the two disagree about ProviderCapability.relations. Read literally, every ProviderCapability is inadmissible and all four live manifests have no id. The repair is the RECORD/MAP distinction above, stated once as a property, and executed at NEG-CLOSED-3.

ADM-DOMAIN.statement: EVERY SCALAR IN A COMMITTED CapabilityManifestV1 IS EITHER BOUND TO A NAMED REGISTRY OR DECLARED OPEN, AND THERE IS NO THIRD STATE. A bound scalar is admitted only if its value is a member of its registry, compared by EXACT NFC UTF-8 BYTES -- no case folding, no alias, no trimming, no prefix match, no normalisation of any kind. An OPEN position is one this schema declares open, with the declaration itself standing as the record that no registry constrains it. A position that is neither bound nor declared open is a schema defect, and it is inadmissible until it is one or the other.
ADM-DOMAIN.whyITISANEWGATEANDNOTACLAUSEOFADMCLOSED: because they quantify over different things. ADM-CLOSED is about which KEYS an object may carry; ADM-DOMAIN is about which VALUES a scalar may hold. The independent review's third channel was reachable precisely because the first property does not reach the second, and folding one into the other would repeat that.
ADM-DOMAIN.boundsSTATED: DL-DOM-1 closes the value-domain channel at the SIX bound positions and declares it OPEN at the EIGHT unbound ones. It does not close the class. See DUD-V4-8.

ADM-ORDER.statement: DL-ORD-1. Every ordered collection in a COMMITTED CapabilityManifestV1 is already in its declared canonical order -- strictly ascending by the unsigned bytewise comparison of its declared sort key's NFC UTF-8 bytes. A committed manifest that is not is REJECTED, with domainReasonCode RELEASE.CAPABILITY_MANIFEST_NOT_CANONICAL. It is never sorted into shape by a consumer.
ADM-ORDER.theSTRUCTURALPROPERTYTHISBUYS: the canonicalising sort is THE IDENTITY on every value that has an id. Three consequences follow as theorems rather than as claims: (a) the set reading and the sequence reading compute the SAME BYTES on every admitted value, so the choice between them is unobservable downstream and cannot be got wrong by an implementer; (b) decode(encode(x)) == x LITERALLY for every admitted x, so injectivity needs no 'on canonical forms' qualifier; (c) two distinct committed documents carrying one id is UNREACHABLE THROUGH A CONFORMING GATE, because at most one of any two differently-ordered documents is admissible.
ADM-ORDER.theWORDINGOFCLAUSEcISNARROWERTHANITSPRED: delivery.v3 wrote 'INEXPRESSIBLE'. Its independent review measured that the state remains COMPUTABLE by an implementer who skips ADM-ORDER -- which is why NEG-ORD-1 and NEG-ORD-2 exist and publish the ids the skipped gate would mint, at a byte length IDENTICAL to the admissible form. 'Unreachable through a conforming gate' is what was bought and is what is now claimed. The narrowing is adopted in full.
ADM-ORDER.whyREJECTANDNOTNORMALISE: silent normalisation is the defect, not the cure. A consumer that sorts is a consumer that turns two logical inputs into one preimage without telling anyone -- the same shape as silently NFC-normalising a string, which resolved-inputs.v2 already forbids in the encoding this recipe uses.
ADM-ORDER.whereCANONICALISATIONISALLOWED: exactly once, in the release builder, on the producer side, BEFORE the id is minted and before the bytes are committed. NEG-ORD-3 executes it.
ADM-ORDER.andTHISISWHYTHELIVEFIXTURESAREINADMISSIB: MEASURED: all four of delivery.v2#installProfiles.profiles[*].capabilityManifest fail ADM-ORDER as written. That is not a defect in them -- installProfiles is an AUTHORING catalogue, not a release. It is stated because a reader who takes those four objects as committed manifests will compute four ids that this artifact does not publish, and because the alternative -- a rule the live corpus already satisfies -- would have been a rule with no live witness.

valueDomains.DL-DOM-1: EVERY SCALAR IN A COMMITTED CapabilityManifestV1 IS EITHER BOUND TO A NAMED REGISTRY OR DECLARED OPEN, AND THERE IS NO THIRD STATE. A bound scalar is admitted only if its value is a member of its registry, compared by EXACT NFC UTF-8 BYTES -- no case folding, no alias, no trimming, no prefix match, no normalisation of any kind. An OPEN position is one this schema declares open, with the declaration itself standing as the record that no registry constrains it. A position that is neither bound nor declared open is a schema defect, and it is inadmissible until it is one or the other.
